title: Goal-family construction bridge
statement: For a selected goal-family candidate, an agent can reconstruct a compact construction bridge that joins the candidate's authored assumptions, existing serving capabilities and implementation routes, and the current Campaign/strategy evidence, so it can choose a bounded next increment and preserve the remaining realization conditions across sessions.

alignment.basis: ADR 0037's domain-general cognitive development and the existing Campaign, strategy, possibility and receipt mechanisms support a construction bridge for a selected candidate.

ambition.basis: Would let a later agent resume a selected capability and distinguish a capability-advancing increment from a local repair.

horizon.basis: Existing possibility, Campaign, strategy, receipt and context records supply the pieces; no bridge implementation exists yet.

realization.basis: No construction-bridge implementation, independent later-agent use or benefit is observed.

synthesis_basis: Combines the one-hop goal-family candidate ecology with construction-time possibility reconciliation and prospective decision memory. It links a selected possibility to existing serving capabilities and current Campaign/strategy evidence while preserving the remaining realization conditions. It is distinct from automatic planning or ranking because the agent selects the candidate, the next increment and the continuation decision.
value_hypothesis: A later agent can resume a selected capability without reconstructing the entire discovery context and can distinguish a capability-advancing increment from a local repair.
revisit_when: A later agent uses the bridge in a real multi-increment construction and either completes the selected capability or finds it redundant with existing Campaign/strategy/handoff context.
counterevidence: Existing Campaign/strategy/handoff surfaces already preserve much of this context; the bridge may be redundant. No independent later-agent use is observed.
claim_ceiling: Proposed integration from one source-grounded synthesis; no implemented bridge, independent use, decision influence, value or authorization.
